result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection equipped with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks, a marked crosswalk, and a traffic signal. While these features provide a baseline level of safety, the wide roadway and lack of physical traffic calming measures may allow for higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Large vehicle obstruction
hazards.description: A large white truck is stopped near the intersection, potentially obscuring sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway near the foreground.

hazards.name: Wide turning radius
hazards.description: The corner geometry allows for relatively fast right turns by vehicles, increasing risk to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and slow turning vehicles by tightening the turn radius.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles receive a green light, increasing visibility.

result.summary: The intersection lacks fundamental pedestrian infrastructure such as marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals, despite its significant width and multi-lane configuration. The environment is heavily oriented toward vehicle throughput, creating a high-exposure environment for anyone attempting to cross.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: No marked crosswalks are provided at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated path of travel.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway in the center foreground and mid-ground.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: There are no visible pedestrian signal heads to indicate when it is safe to cross relative to vehicle traffic phases.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corners of the intersection where vehicle signals are mounted.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway creates a long exposure time for pedestrians, increasing the risk of conflict with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: The entire width of the multi-lane roadway.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks on all legs of the intersection to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The environment features a signalized intersection with a 'No Turn on Red' restriction, which provides some protection for pedestrians. However, the absence of visible marked crosswalks and dedicated pedestrian signals at this residential intersection increases the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted crosswalk markings, making the intended pedestrian path unclear to motorists.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection area in the center-left background

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide sufficient clearance time.
hazards.location_in_image: Traffic signal poles at the intersection

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads with Countdown
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to improve predictability and safety for people crossing.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.

result.summary: The environment features a well-maintained sidewalk buffered by mature trees and a dedicated bike lane, providing good separation for pedestrians. However, the crossing lacks active signalization and has a relatively wide exposure distance across multiple lane types.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A large utility pole is positioned close to the intersection, potentially blocking the view of pedestrians for oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground near the sidewalk edge.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk
hazards.description: The painted crosswalk markings are somewhat worn and lack high-visibility patterns, reducing their effectiveness.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Upgrade the existing transverse markings to a continental or ladder pattern to increase visibility to drivers.

interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corner to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve sightlines by moving pedestrians further into the driver's field of view.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-activated flashing lights to alert drivers of people waiting to cross at this unsignalized location.
